newsitem.title: LEBANON: Ceasefire group deplores Israel shelling of Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Ceasefire group deplores Israel shelling of Lebanon.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon said on Thursday Israeli forces were responsible for shelling two villages on Saturday and deplored the wounding of six civilians in the bombardment.

The group, comprising the United States, France, Israel, Lebanon and Syria, said in a statement it "deplored by unanimity the injuries caused to Lebanese civilians and the damage to houses in the villages of Kfar Tibnit and Nabatiyet el-Fawka" on December 7.
It was the third time in succession that the monitoring group has held Israel responsible for shelling a south Lebanon village and the second time it has "deplored" the Israeli actions.

The statement followed four days of meetings on a Lebanese complaint over the shelling which, according to security sources, followed an attack by Moslem guerrillas that killed an Israeli soldier and wounded another.

"The Group further acknowledged as fact that during Israeli firing following the side bomb attack, one Israeli flechette round injured six Lebanese civilians, and the Monitoring group considered that Israeli forces are responsible for their firing procedures," the statement added.
U.N. officials say the anti-personnel flechette shells, which spray dozens of steel darts, are banned internationally.
The multinational monitoring group was formed under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement of April 26 that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in which 200 people were killed.

On November 6, it held Israel responsible for shelling the village of Louwaizeh, wounding a woman. On October 18, the monitors "deplored" an Israeli bombardment which wounded 13 civilians in the village of Safad al-Batikh.
The ceasefire agreement forbids all attacks from or at civilian areas but does not bar guerrilla raids on Israeli forces in south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.
The monitoring group hold its meetings at the coastal headquarters of the U.N. peacekeeping force in south Lebanon at Naqoura in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
